items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We all did most of it in one take apiece... That’s with Freddie. Freddie Freeloader. He stopped. I think he said, “Don’t play A-flat,” or whatever that chord was. But that was – we played that again... The whole date went like that.

ctx.x: Put the grease in it. Bill could do it. He probably couldn’t do it like Wynton did. It’s two different styles. That’s what he wanted. So that’s what happened. That’s how it all came about. We all did most of it in one take apiece, because he didn’t like to go over things, because he figured that was – every time you do it, it would probably get worse. He liked the first out-of-the-barrel kind of thing. So that’s how most of it happened, except for the tune that Wynton played on. He stopped that, because there was…

Freddie Freeloader. He stopped. I think he said, “Don’t play A-flat,” or whatever that chord was. But that was – we played that again, and that was that. The whole date went like that.
